reasons: Rule correctly applied: the cited Section 4 paragraphs cover only term, notice and the Termination Payment, and no transition, data-return, export or deletion language appears, so a 'missing' finding with an inserted clause is the right treatment for a hosting agreement where HDI holds Company Content, user and order data.

The inserted Section 4.3 tracks the playbook's preferred position closely (up to six months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, machine-readable return of Company data within thirty days of the Termination Date, and certified deletion thereafter) and is drafted in the direction favorable to us as the Customer/Company.

Placement at the end of Section 4 (appended after the final Termination Payment subsection) is the natural home for exit mechanics, and the edit is purely additive with no alteration of existing text, i.e. the smallest edit that reaches the position.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required [Playbook] prefix, explains the gap and the added obligations, and offers the 90-day fallback with the same thirty-day export.
Minor, non-blocking: the new clause is numbered 4.3 on the assumption no existing 4.3 follows the Termination Payment subsections; confirm numbering against the full Section 4 before issuing.
